task:
Certainly, <Ranger>! We have a special mission for you:
Both humans and pelengs are very fond of fishing. It's a tradition that goes back for centuries, but nobody is sure where it originated. Rumor has it that it was invented by humans on a planet called Earth some 3000 years ago. Back then it was not a hobby - it was an occupation. However, faeyan scientists insist that this is false. Anyway, let's stay focused. The 96th Fishing Championship will soon be held on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> star system. This year the ballot dictates that we send a ranger to the championship. We want you to represent us. It will take place on <Date>, so you'll need to be there before then. And if you win, we'll thank you with a lavish <Money> cr.
success: Oh! Hello, ranger <Ranger>! Nice to see you again! You’re known as one of the best ever fishermen. Our citizens regard you a true hero. Our planet's prestige has shot through the roof because of your brilliant victory. Your heroics have earned you your reward of <Money> cr.
loc.1.0:
You arrive on planet <ToPlanet>. It's identical to other planets of this class except for its rich flora. Upon reaching the championship venue, you look around and notice that there aren't any faeyan boats - only human and peleng. Some peleng walks down a ramp to your right. Hordes of journalists besiege him, clamoring for an interview. "He must be some big cheese," you think.
Just then, a small, round-shouldered man comes up to you.
"Are you ranger <Ranger>, here to represent planet <FromPlanet>?" he asks.
"Yes, that's me." you reply.
"Ha, ha!... Do you really think you stand a chance against Vulture?" he asks, pointing back at the peleng being mobbed by reporters. "Anyway, you don't have to answer that. Come on, I'll show you to your hut."
loc.2.0:
You walk for a short time. Your guide leads you to your night's lodgings. It wasn't what you had dreamed of, but it'll do for one night. You enter the hut. The room is poorly furnished: There's an old sofa under the window to the right and a wardrobe to the left. Above the one-legged table standing near the wardrobe is a bamboo fishing rod.
"These are your chambers," says the guide, delving into his pockets for money. "My boss told me to give you eight hundred marks," he says and holds out a wad of <clr>800<clrEnd> marks. "You can use them to buy something at the stand across the street. If you have any questions, ask quickly – I'm in a hurry."
loc.2.1: "There is a bar not far from here. All the fishermen in the region go there to drink."
loc.2.2:
"The competition's host planet is determined each year by lot. The competition rules were made up a long time ago. They're very simple. 
At dawn, participants are distributed around the lake. You have a little time to prepare – about 10 minutes. Then you have to wait for the maloq's starting shot. If you start fishing before that, you'll be immediately disqualified. They are very strict about this! You have exactly 30 minutes to fish from the time of the starting shot.  When the time is up, your catch is weighed. The fisherman with the heaviest catch wins. That's all. And good luck - you'll need it."
loc.2.3:
"This peleng is an absolute champion. He's won the competition five times in a row. He's a real master at what he does. When Vulture fishes, it's almost as if the fish are choosing to leap toward him onto the shore. Amazing, isn't it? Many participants no longer enter the competition, because they see no point in competing with him. Some even tried to frighten him away from the competition. But the more they intimidated him, the less of an effect it had on him. Everybody knows he has some secret, but they can't figure out what it is. The organizers have scrutinized his actions during the competition, but they've found nothing that breaks the rules. This peleng is probably just very lucky. Good luck, <Ranger>. You're going to need it in your struggle with Vulture.
Any questions? Ask quickly, I've got a lot to do!"
loc.4.0: You're standing in the middle of your hut. You are in familiar territory: an old sofa, a wardrobe, and a one-legged table. A fishing rod hangs above the table. It's not very well equipped, but you could fish with it... There's a portrait of some strange peleng hanging on the wall. In short, you feel entirely at home.
loc.9.0:
<clr>FISHING MANUAL<clrEnd>.
Do you want to learn how to fish, where to fish, and how to choose your bait? Then you may be interested in the following:
<clr>Cheric<clrEnd>
What do you need to catch a cheric? It doesn't take anything special. The cheric is a small, oblong fish that lives in the shallows. It's quite forgiving – it'll bite anything that can be bitten. It inhabits and breeds primarily among the reeds. The average adult cheric weighs 300 g.
<clr>Murlock<clrEnd>
You need good fishing tackle to catch a murlock. The murlock is a medium-sized, ball-shaped fish that often swims in the shallows on the hunt for cherics. It also likes white worms. An adult murlock weighs 400-600 g.
<clr>Wolt<clrEnd>
You'll need a good fishing rod and tackle to catch a wolt. The wolt is a large, regular-shaped fish. It generally inhabits deep locations; it avoids places with a lot of reeds. It only feeds on green worms. Adult specimens weigh from 700 g to 1000 g.
loc.11.0:
The vegetation in this small town is stunning. High trees, overgrown alleyways... These plants are everywhere!
You're standing in the middle of the road. In front of you, there is a stand called "Fishermen Never Sleep", and your hut is behind you. To your left, the road heads uphill, while to the right it leads downhill. In the distance, you notice the silver lake where you'll be fishing. All around the passersby are excitedly talking about the upcoming championship. Where do you want to go?
loc.12.0: You go down to the lake. You are met by an awful sight: There's just mud here – hardly any greenery at all. But the silence here calms your soul, which suffered so much during the war with the dominators. "This must be where the contest will take place," you thought.
loc.13.0:
You walk down the road and see a bar with broken windows and battered door. Two pelengs are standing on the stoop, smoking weed. 
"Ha! Poor Vulture...I'm going to catch more than he ever has!" cries one of them, while the other nods after each utterance.
loc.14.0: You go into the stand. An old gaal is at the counter. His black cap has a hole in the forehead for his third eye, and he's wearing a yellow t-shirt with Greenpeace emblazoned across the front! He spots you and his eyes light up in the hopes that you'll buy something.
loc.14.1: You are in the stand. An old gaal is at the counter. His black cap has a hole in the forehead for his third eye, and he's wearing a yellow t-shirt with Greenpeace emblazoned across the front! He spots you and his eyes light up in the hopes that you'll buy something.
loc.23.0: You come to a small aquarium filled with clean, clear water. There are some strange, dark-green creatures covered with bubbles swimming inside. They mill about emitting hardly-audible squeaks. A sign hangs below:  "<clr>One worm costs 3 marks <clrEnd>"
loc.24.0:
There is a selection of various fishing rods in front of you. The gaal stands near the rods and makes a sales pitch.
The <clr>Reflex<clrEnd> fishing rod is a wonderful tool – one of the best fishing rods ever created. It works wonders in the hands of a master fisherman! It was designed and manufactured for professionals by the peleng company Tsakhta Piyakhta.
The <clr>Aqua<clrEnd> fishing rod is the most popular rod among amateur fishermen. You can catch any kind of fish with it. And you can fish anywhere in the galaxy with this rod. It is made by the Antifish solar system.
The <clr>Cotton<clrEnd> fishing rod is an old telescoping model. Retired pelengs usually buy this kind. There's nothing better for stationary fishing, which nearly no one is interested in. It's manufactured by the Fishermen's Union.
And then there's the <clr>Filter<clrEnd> fishing rod. This useless piece of crap was designed by gaalian engineers. Nobody wants to buy it, but the intergalactic council ordered that the product must be distributed to the populated planets of the galaxy. Made by Greenpeace.
loc.25.0: You come up to a container directly in front of you. You can see countless translucent white worms – all actively creeping about. They're nearly jumping out of the metal barrel. You notice a sign above your head that reads: "<clr>One worm costs 2 marks<clrEnd>".
loc.26.0: In a dark corner, you find an old aluminum basin filled with something. You come closer and see a heap of old, stinky worms. Nothing special here - these are the simple segmented worms that your grandfather used as bait. A piece of paper lying in the basin indicates the price: "<clr>One worm costs 1 mark<clrEnd>"
loc.27.0:
Select the right fishing tackle: 
- <clr>Transparent line and a titanium hook<clrEnd> - A transparent line is absolutely invisible in the water for fish and every other intelligent species in our galaxy. A titanium hook can withstand any fish. It's also very light, so worms can easily twist and spin on it.
- <clr>Fishing tackle combo: thin line and a sharp hook<clrEnd> - This is a winning combination; it can hold even a heavy fish.
- <clr>Ordinary line and ordinary hook<clrEnd> - This is a commodity available everywhere.
- <clr>Fishing tackle combo: thick line and blunt, rusty hook<clrEnd> - Developed by Greenpeace, our favorite manufacturer.
 In most cases, this fishing tackle simply frightens the fish away.
loc.28.0:
The man looks at you scornfully with one eye. He turns red with anger and curses you loudly, stamping and kicking the hull of your ship. After a couple of minutes, he had tenderized his leg and began shouting even louder.
"To hell with fishing," you think. You get aboard your ship and fly away from the planet.
loc.30.0:
You lie on the sofa, contemplating the competition tomorrow. The main question in your mind is whether or not the great ranger <Ranger> can beat this invincible Vulture. In your pondering, you didn't realize that you have fallen asleep. The night passes calmly and without incident. 
As you wake up, you can see beams of light streaming through your little window. You stretch, get out of bed, and get dressed quickly. It's a beautiful morning for fishing. You slept well, and now you're ready to win the competition.
loc.31.0: You are near the bar with the broken windows. The door is beaten in. Pelengs are standing on the stoop, smoking weed.
loc.32.0: You're standing in a smoky bar. There are a lot of drunk fishermen discussing tomorrow’s competition. You can hear the name <clr>Vulture<clrEnd> in their conversations from time to time. A lot of people are crowding around a table where somebody's playing dice.
loc.32.1: You get up from the bar. What will you do now?
loc.32.2: You leave the gamblers. What next?
loc.32.3: No! Why try if you don't know if you can win? A space pilot's work is exhausting and affects muscle mass.
loc.32.4: You drop your head and walk away from Vulture, who is smiling proudly. What are you going to do next?
loc.32.5: You walk away from Vulture proudly, feeling like a victor. The others in the bar watch you go out with a smile.  You feel like doing something like this again, so what's next?
loc.32.6: You're standing in a smoky bar. There are a lot of drunk fishermen discussing tomorrow’s competition. You can hear the name <clr>Vulture<clrEnd> in their conversations from time to time. A lot of people are crowding around a table where somebody's playing dice.
loc.36.0: You push your way through to the people playing dice. The crowd around the table is huge.
loc.36.1: You leave the gambling table, but the others continue playing.
loc.37.0:
You take a seat at the table. There are swarthy people sitting around, watching you.
"The table stakes are <clr>20 marks<clrEnd>," says one.
"These are the rules of the game," adds another. "We take turns rolling the dice. The highest roll wins the pot. Everybody pays the winner <clr>20 marks<clrEnd>. If two people get the same roll, then it's a draw. They keep their own money and get <clr>10 marks<clrEnd> from the others. Got it?"
You nod.
loc.41.0: You're sitting at the table, gambling.
loc.44.0:
Vulture looks at you, his right eye twitching.
"Ah! I think I know you!" he cries. "You're ranger <Ranger> – I've heard about you. 
Do you really think you can win the competition? Nothing works out for you. I've been the winner for five years in a row. And I'm going to win again this time."
He looks you over again from bottom to top and says,
"Wanna arm wrestle? The loser pays <clr>100 marks<clrEnd> to the winner. Agreed?"
loc.45.0:
You sit at a table and grip Vulture's hand. Your eyes meet. He looks at you confidently, smiles, and spits on the ground enthusiastically. At present, you're thinking only of victory - not of winning the fishing competition, but of beating Vulture in this arm wrestling match.
"Begin wrestling on the count of three," says a small fae standing nearby.
Focusing all your strength in your fists, you grip Vulture's hand and prepare yourself.
"One... Two... Three... Go!!!"
loc.49.0:
You again come up to Vulture.
"Well? Are you going to wrestle with me?" Vulture asks.
loc.49.1:
You come up to the peleng once again. He gave a vicious look with his eyes.
"Is there something else you need?" Vulture asks.
loc.51.0:
People get up from the table and the crowd disperses.
You win!!!
loc.53.0:
When you leave your hut, you find a man who met you at the spaceport is already waiting for you. He's wearing coveralls and has a net on his head. Behind him, you can see crowds of people moving along the road. Someone screams, "Vulture's the best!"
"Finally!" cries the man. "Come along. I'll show you the way."
You arrive at the lake. There are stands with everything you could possibly want. Hundreds of cameras fly overhead, tracking the participants' every move. Journalists are interviewing the planet's president. 
Your guide points at a cliff near the water. 
"This is where you start," he says and then leaves.
You take your place. There had been tremendous noise for about 20 minutes. Then a siren let out an unexpected blast, and all was quiet.
"I should get ready," you think to yourself.
You prepare everything you need and wait another five minutes.  At last, a maloq floating above the water on some kind of disc, shoots some sort of antediluvian gun... The time has come.
loc.54.0: The lake looks rather beautiful from here. There’s a small cliff, average depth, no reeds. That makes this a good place for wolts.
loc.55.0: You descend to the water's edge. The lake is calm here. The water level is low and the bank is a bit reedy. It’s ideal for murlocks.
loc.56.0: You carefully approach the water along the gently sloping shore. The bright sunlight blinds you. Taking a closer look, you determine the lake has an average depth here. The bank is very reedy, which is certain to attract cherics and small murlocks.
loc.57.0: You move quickly to the water's edge. The water is surprisingly dark, indicating it is quite deep. The bank is a little reedy, but it's still good for catching big fish.
loc.58.0: You move across the cliff very slowly and carefully. You see a small murlock in the clear water. It's shallow here and there are no reeds on the shore. That means there might be wolts!
loc.59.0: You are standing before an abrupt dropoff. The current is strong here and the waters dark. It must be very deep here – you can't see a single reed. This shore is perfect for wolts.
loc.60.0: You approach the precipice. There's not much current and the water is dark, which means it's deep here. The shore is perfectly clean, not a reed in sight. There could be some good wolts and murlocks here.
loc.61.0: You're at the cliff, attracted by the water's calm appearance. Upon closer inspection, you determine that the lake has an average depth here. There are a few reeds nearby. It wouldn't be a bad place to catch murlocks and cherics.
loc.62.0: You carefully approach the water along the gently sloping shore. The water near the shore is as clear as glass, but it becomes dark rather abruptly a bit farther out. Taking a closer look around, you determine that the lake has an average depth here. The bank is very reedy, but it’s an ideal place for cherics and small murlocks.
loc.63.0: You move across a sharp decent to get a bit closer to the water. The water is calm and the view of the lake is excellent. Upon closer inspection, you determine that the lake has an average depth here. There are some dense reeds. This is an obvious habitat for decent murlocks.

loc.128.0:
Your catch is weighed. It is [p9] g more than the rest!
Vulture only took in [p10] g.
There can be no doubt about it - you win. You are given a great-looking cup with your name – <Ranger> – engraved on it in gold letters. Crowds of journalists come running up and ask strange questions. The competition's main judge gives you a check for [p35] cr. 
You give interviews with pleasure and decide to celebrate your victory. The nearest place to go is the bar with the broken windows, so you head there. You have a great time. Then you return to your godforsaken hut, since you are in no condition to depart today. After collapsing onto the sofa, you fall asleep. In the morning you pack quickly, feeling fresh and full of energy. You head to the spaceport, where you successfully cash your check. Then you take a seat in your spacecraft and fly away.

loc.150.0: Feeling bitter, Vulture sits before you and glares. Clearly, he has no intention of losing to you. Right now all your thoughts are concentrated on Vulture's hand. Victory is the only thing on your mind.
loc.152.0:
Your catch is weighed. It is [p9] g. Vulture's catch is weighed and it is...  also [p10] g!
The judges are confused. The two leading fishermen have never before tied at the weighing. They decide to let both contestants take first place.
Both of you are given a great-looking cup with your names engraved on it in gold letters. Crowds of journalists come running up and ask strange questions. The competition's main judge gives you a check for [p35] cr. 
You and Vulture give interviews with pleasure, pose together for photos, and decide to celebrate your joint victory. The nearest place to go is the bar with the broken windows, so you head there. You have a great time socializing with other fired-up men. Then you return to your godforsaken hut, since you are in no condition to depart today. The next morning you pack quickly, feeling fresh and full of energy. You head to the spaceport, where you successfully cash your check. Then you take a seat in your spacecraft and fly away.
loc.153.0: You struggle tooth and nail and tighten your muscles. Sensing your advantage over Vulture, you prevailed against him - even though he's a formidable opponent. Looking at his defeated eyes, you demand your money. Vulture unwillingly handed over a <clr>100-mark<clrEnd> bill.
loc.153.1:
You struggle tooth and nail, but... The peleng still takes the cake!
With a telling look, he reminds you about the money.
